While I'm a top priority applicant at y, the sheer number of other applicants who also prefer y might mean I get rejected. My ranking at w is also 1st, which gives me a strong chance there. Given the general preference for y, w might be less competitive than y. If I am rejected from y, w becomes a very strong fallback option.

Z and x are both 2nd priority for me. Since my value for z is higher than x, and it's likely that z will be less competitive than x due to the overall applicant preferences, I should rank z ahead of x.

Therefore, my ranking will be y > z > w > x. This maximizes my chances of getting my highest value school (y), while still positioning me well for alternative options (z, w, x) should I be rejected from my top choices.
